examInfo.format: 12 Single Choice + 4 Multiple Choice (Prüfungsstil, mit Rechenfragen)
examInfo.grading: Übungsset ohne Note — Ziel: ≥ 60 % der Punkte

questions.text: Which condition is typically NOT favourable for revenue management?

choices.text: Perishable capacity (unsold seats have no value after the event)
Constant demand and high marginal cost per additional customer
Segmentable demand with different willingness to pay
Fixed capacity in the short term

questions.explanation: RM braucht verderbliche Kapazität, segmentierbare Nachfrage, kurzfristig fixe Kapazität, volatile Nachfrage und niedrige Grenzkosten. Konstante Nachfrage und hohe Grenzkosten sprechen dagegen.

questions.text:
Five potential customers have the following willingness to pay (WTP): CHF 6, 8, 10, 12 and 15. A customer buys if WTP ≥ price.

Which single price maximises the revenue?

A survey covering 1 % of the target market (40 respondents) shows that 12 respondents would buy at a price of CHF 90.

How large is the market demand at CHF 90?
questions.explanation: Market Demand = Sample Demand / Anteil = 12 / 0.01 = 1'200. Excel: Sample Demand =COUNTIF(WTP; ">="&Preis).

questions.text:
The demand is linear: D(p) = 1'000 − 10·p, the marginal cost is zero and the capacity is 400 units.

Which price should be set?
questions.explanation: Unbeschränktes Umsatzmaximum bei p = a/(2b) = 50 mit D = 500 > Kapazität 400. Deshalb Preis, bei dem D = 400: p = (1'000 − 400)/10 = 60.

questions.text:
The demand follows D(p) = a·e^(−0.002·p) with zero marginal cost.

Which price maximises the revenue?
questions.explanation: Umsatz p·a·e^(−bp): Ableitung ergibt p* = 1/b = 1/0.002 = 500. Mit Grenzkosten c wäre p* = c + 1/b.

questions.text:
Littlewood: high fare p_H = CHF 200, low fare p_L = CHF 50, demand of the high-fare class D_H ~ N(80, 20²), capacity 150.

How many seats should be protected for the high fare (z = 0.674 for 75 %)?

A flight has 100 seats and a show-up rate of 95 %. The airline accepts 105 bookings.

How many passengers are expected to show up?
questions.explanation: 105 · 0.95 = 99.75. Das Risiko, dass mehr als 100 erscheinen, hängt von der Streuung ab (Binomial); Overbooking bis P(Shows ≥ C) ≤ p/(p + c_d).

questions.text:
Four customers have WTP for product A: 10, 2, 6, 5 and for product B: 2, 10, 5, 6. All costs are zero.

What is the maximum total revenue of pure bundling (one price for A + B)?
questions.explanation: Bundle-WTP: 12, 12, 11, 11 ⇒ Preis 11 ⇒ alle 4 kaufen ⇒ 44. Einzeln: A bester Preis 5 ⇒ 15, B ebenso 15 ⇒ 30. Bündelung lohnt hier wegen der negativ korrelierten WTP.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a valid segmentation criterion (fence) for price differentiation?

choices.text: Booking time (early bird vs. last minute)

questions.explanation: Gültige Fences: Region, Produktvariante, Buchungszeitpunkt, Flexibilität, Kanal. Religion/Ethnizität sind diskriminierend und unzulässig.

questions.text:
In a bundling or two-part-tariff spreadsheet, a customer's WTP minus the price is negative for one option.

How should this value be treated?

choices.text: Set to 0, because the customer simply does not buy that option
Keep it negative, because it reduces the revenue
Delete the customer from the sample

questions.explanation: Negative Konsumentenrente ⇒ Kauf findet nicht statt ⇒ Wert 0 (=MAX(0; WTP−Preis)). Typische Fehlerstelle bei Mixed Bundling und Two-Part Tariff.

questions.text: Which sentence about the relationship between overbooking and the newsvendor logic is correct?

choices.text: Overbooking only makes sense if all passengers show up
Overbooking follows newsvendor logic: Cu = revenue of an empty seat, Co = cost of denied service
Overbooking is limited to physical products
Overbooking has nothing to do with the newsvendor model

questions.explanation: Weitere Buchung annehmen, solange P(Shows ≥ C) ≤ p/(p + c_d): Der leere Platz entspricht den Underage-Kosten, die Verweigerung den Overage-Kosten.

questions.text: An airline sells economy tickets at CHF 120 and business tickets at CHF 400 for the same flight. Which concept does this illustrate?
questions.explanation: Zwei Produktvarianten für Segmente mit unterschiedlicher Zahlungsbereitschaft, abgesichert durch Leistungsunterschiede (Fence).

sections.title: Part B – Multiple Choice (4 Points)
sections.description: At least two answers are correct. Only the complete correct combination scores (no partial points).

questions.text: When is revenue management typically used?

choices.text: Capacity is fixed in the short term
Marginal costs of an additional customer are low

questions.explanation: Voraussetzungen: nicht lagerbar, segmentierbar, fixe Kapazität, niedrige Grenzkosten, volatile Nachfrage. Konstante Nachfrage ist keine Voraussetzung.

questions.text: Which statements about revenue management are correct?

choices.text: It assumes that demand depends on the price.
Product bundling is one of the classic methods.
It is limited to product companies, because services cannot be stored.
It refers to methods for optimising revenue and profit.
It is especially relevant for services such as airlines and hotels.

questions.explanation: Definition und Preisabhängigkeit der Nachfrage sind zentral; Product Bundling ist klassisch; RM ist besonders für Dienstleistungen relevant (nicht lagerbar), nicht auf Produktunternehmen beschränkt.

questions.text: Which statements about valid fences are correct?

choices.text: Booking lead time is a valid fence.
Geographic location or a verified student status can be used as a fence.
Income is always an easily enforceable fence.
Religion is a valid fence as long as it is easy to verify.
Ticket flexibility (refundable vs. non-refundable) is a valid fence.

questions.explanation: Gültig: Buchungszeitpunkt, Flexibilität, Geografie/Status. Religion ist diskriminierend; Einkommen ist schwer verifizierbar und rechtlich heikel.

questions.text: Which statements about bundling and non-linear pricing are correct?

choices.text: A two-part tariff consists of a fixed fee and a usage-dependent price.
In pure bundling the single products are also offered separately.
Bundling is most profitable when the WTPs of the products are negatively correlated.
Bundling is never profitable if customers have different WTPs.
In mixed bundling the bundle and the single products are offered.

questions.explanation: Negative Korrelation der WTP macht Bündelung attraktiv; Mixed Bundling = beides; Two-Part Tariff = Grundgebühr + Nutzungspreis. Pure Bundling bietet gerade keine Einzelprodukte.
